mechanism_narrative: IGF1R (RTK) and IL6ST/gp130 (cytokine receptor) are co-expressed in aged skeletal muscle (MF-I, MF-II, FB, MuSC). The flexible_GS4 linker (~20 Å) forces close proximity between IGF1R's tyrosine kinase domain and IL6ST's JAK-associated intracellular domain. Under forced co-clustering, IGF1R's kinase transphosphorylates IL6ST's cytoplasmic tyrosines (especially Y759, Y767, Y814, Y905), creating docking sites for STAT3 and PTPN11/SHP2 that are normally only engaged by JAK-mediated IL6ST phosphorylation. Simultaneously, IL6ST-associated JAKs (JAK1/JAK2) transphosphorylate IGF1R's activation loop tyrosines (Y1161/Y1165/Y1166), amplifying IRS1/IRS2 recruitment and PI3K-AKT signaling beyond normal IGF1R activation levels. The biased output is a hybrid IGF1R->PI3K/AKT + IL6ST->STAT3 signal with enhanced MAPK/ERK via GRB2-SHC1-SOS-RAS, while PLCgamma (PLCG1/PLCG2) is sterically excluded due to the asymmetric ECD geometry (IGF1R ECD=195aa vs IL6ST ECD=597aa, ratio 3.06x) and CBL-mediated negative regulation is suppressed, shifting the balance toward pro-survival/pro-differentiation transcriptional programs that oppose the aged muscle phenotype.
